questions.q: A water tank has the shape of an inverted right circular cone, whose semi-vertical angle is $\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) .$ Water is poured into it at a constant rate of $5cubicm / min .$~Then the rate $($in $m / min ) ,$~at which the level of water is rising at the instant when the depth of water in the tank is $10m;$ is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The given water tank is of the shape shown by the diagram.

The semi-vertical angle& $\theta = \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right), ⇒ tan\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Let at any time $tmin,$ height of water level is $hm$~ and radius of cone filled with water be $rm .$

Also, we have~$tan\theta = \dfrac{r}{h}$

$⇒ \dfrac{r}{h} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{h}{2} . . . \left(i\right)$

Now, the volume of the water at time~$tmin$ in the cone is~$V = $\dfrac{1}{3}\pir^{2}$h$

On putting the value of~$r$~from the equation~\left(i\right),$~we get

$V = $\dfrac{π}{3} $\left(\dfrac{h3}{4}) = \dfrac{π}{12} \left($h^{3}\right)$

Now, differentiating with respect to~$t,$~we get

\dfrac{dV}{dt} = \dfrac{π}{12}$⋅ \left($3h^{2}\dfrac{dh}{dt}\right)$

Put the given value of~$\dfrac{dV}{dt} \text{ and } h$

$⇒ 5 = \dfrac{π}{4}⋅ $\left(100\dfrac{dh}{dt})

$⇒ $\dfrac{dh}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{5\pi}$m / min$

$

questions.q: If $x = 1$ is a critical point of the function $f ( x ) = \left(3x^{2} + ax - 2 - a\right)e^{x},$ then&
options: $x = 1$ and$x = - \dfrac{2}{3}$ is a local maxima of $f$
$x = 1$ is a local maxima and$x = - \dfrac{2}{2}$ is a local minima of $f$
$x = 1$~is a~local~minima and$x = - \dfrac{2}{3}$ are local maxima of $f$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$f ( x ) = \left(3x^{2} + ax - 2 - a\right)e^{x}$
$f ' ( x ) = \left(3x^{2} + ax - 2 - a\right)e^{x} + e^{x} ( 6x + a ) = e^{x}\left(3x^{2} + ( a + 6 ) x - 2\right)$

$∵ x = 1$ is a critical point $∴ f^{'} ( 1 ) = 0$

$∴ 3 + a + 6 - 2 = 0$
$a = - 7$

$∴ f^{'} ( x ) = e^{x}\left(3x^{2} - x - 2\right) = e^{x}\left(3x^{2} - 3x + 2x - 2\right) = e^{x} ( 3x + 2 ) ( x - 1 )$

$∴$ maxima at $x = $\dfrac{- 2}{3}$∴$ minima at $x = 1

$

questions.q: Let $g \left(x\right) = f  \left($x\right) + f \left(1 - x\right) and $f^{"} \left(x\right) > 0, x \in  \left(0, 1\right)$. If $g$ is decreasing in the interval  \left($0, $\alpha\right)~and increasing in the interval \left(\alpha,$1\right)$, then $\tan^{- 1}$2\alpha + \tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{1}{α}) + \tan^{- 1} $\left(\dfrac{\alpha + 1}{α})is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$g \left(x\right) = f \left($x\right) + f \left(1 - x\right)$ and $f^{"} \left(x\right) > 0, x \in \left(0, 1\right)$. If $g$ is decreasing in the interval \left($0, $\alpha\right)~and increasing in the interval \left(\alpha,$1\right)$,

Now solving,

$g \left($x\right) = f \left($x\right) + f \left(1 - x\right)$

Now differentiating both side we get,

$g^{'} \left(x\right) = f^{'} \left($x\right) - f^{'}\left($1 - x\right)$

Differentiating again we get,

$g^{"} \left(x\right) = f^{"} \left(x\right) + f^{"} \left($1 - x\right) > 0$

So,~$g^{'}\left($x\right)$ is increasing as given~$f^{"} \left($x\right) > 0$

$⇒ g^{'}\left($0\right) < g^{'}\left(1\right)$

$⇒ f^{'} \left($0\right) - f^{'} \left($1\right) < f^{'}\left(1\right) - f^{'}\left(0\right)$

$⇒ f^{'} \left($0\right) < f^{'} \left(1\right)$

Now finding~$g^{'} \left($x\right) = 0$~we get,

$⇒ f^{'}\left($x\right) = f^{'}\left($1 - x\right)$

$⇒ x = 1 - x$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Now~$g^{'} \left($x\right)$ is positive for~$x \in \left(0, $\dfrac{1}{2}\right)

And~$g^{'} \left($x\right)$ is negative for $x \in \left(\dfrac{1}{2},1\right)$

$∴ \alpha = \dfrac{1}{2}$

So,~

$\tan^{- 1}2\alpha + \tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{1}{α}\right) + \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\alpha + 1}{α}\right)

$= \tan^{- 1}1 + \tan^{- 1}2 + \tan^{- 1}3$

=\dfrac{π}{4} + \tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{2 + 3}{1 - 6}\right)

=\dfrac{π}{4} + \tan^{- 1}\left(-$1\right)$

$= \dfrac{π}{4} + \dfrac{3\pi}{4} = \pi$

questions.q: The sum of the abosolute maximum and minimum values of the function $f \left(x\right) =  \left|$x^{2} - 5x + 6\right| - 3x + 2$ in the interval \left[-$1, 3\right]$ is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \left|x^{2} - 5x + 6\right| - 3x + 2$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left|\left(x - 3\right)\left(x - 2\right)\right| - 3x + 2$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left\{$\begin{cases}x^{2} - 8x + 8 & ; x \in \left[-1, 2\right] \\ - x^{2} + 2x - 4 & ; x \in ( 2, 3 ]\end{cases}$\right

$⇒ f^{'}\left(x\right) = \left\{$\begin{cases}2x - 8 & ; x \in \left(-1, 2\right) \\ - x + 2 & ; x \in \left(2, 3\right)\end{cases}$\right

Now point of extrema will be~$2x - 8 = 0 ⇒ x = 4$which is not in domain~and~$- x + 2 = 0 ⇒ x = 2$

Now for finding the value of global~minima and maxima we will check the value of function at extrema points~and boundary points,

So,~$f\left(x\right) = x^{2} - 8x + 8$~will give,~$f\left(-1\right) = 17 \text{ and } f\left(2\right) = - 4$

And~$f\left(x\right) = - x^{2} + 2x - 4$~will give,~$f\left(2\right) = 4, f\left(3\right) = - 7$

Hence, absolute minima is~$- 7$~and maxima is~$17$

So, their sum is~$- 7 + 17 = 10

$

questions.q: A wire of length $22m$& is to be cut into two pieces. One of the pieces is to be made into a square and the other into an equilateral triangle. Then, the length of the side of the equilateral triangle, so that the combined area of the square and the equilateral triangle is minimum, is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the side& of square& be& $\dfrac{22 - l}{4}$~and side of triangle be~$\dfrac{l}{3}$~,

So, total area is given by $\Delta = \dfrac{3}{4}\left(\dfrac{l}{3}\right)2 + \left(\dfrac{22 - l}{4}\right)2$

$⇒ \Delta = \dfrac{1}{12\sqrt{3}} \cdot l^{2} + \dfrac{1}{16}\left(22 - l\right)2$

Differentiating with respect to $l$~to get maxima and minima points,

$⇒ \dfrac{d\Delta}{dl} = \dfrac{1}{6\sqrt{3}} \cdot l - \dfrac{1}{8}\left(22 - l\right) = 0$~$⇒ l = \dfrac{66\sqrt{3}}{4 + 3\sqrt{3}}$

Also$\dfrac{d^{2}\Delta}{dl^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{6\sqrt{3}} + \dfrac{1}{8}$ ($+ ve$. which is case of minima)

So, side~of triangle will be~$= \dfrac{l}{3} = \dfrac{22\sqrt{3}}{4 + 3\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{66}{4\sqrt{3} + 9}$

questions.q: The number of real roots of the equation $e^{6x} - e^{4x} - 2e^{3x} - 12e^{2x} + e^{x} + 1 = 0$ is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$e^{6x} - e^{4x} - 2e^{3x} - 12e^{2x} + e^{x} + 1 = 0$

\left(e^{3x}\right)2 - 2e^{3x} + 1 - e^{4x} + e^{x} = 12e^{2x}$

$⇒ \left(e^{3x} - 1\right)2 - e^{x}\left(e^{3x} - 1\right) = 12e^{2x}$

$⇒ \left(e^{3x} - 1\right)\left(e^{3x} - 1 - e^{x}\right) = 12e^{2x}$

$⇒ \left(e^{3x} - 1 - e^{x}\right)e^{2x} = 12\left(e^{3x} - 1\right)$

$⇒ e^{x} - e^{- x} - e^{- 2x} = $\dfrac{12}{e^{3x} - 1}

Assume,~$f\left(x\right) = e^{x} - e^{- x} - e^{- 2x} \text{ and } g\left(x\right) = $\dfrac{12}{e^{3x} - 1}

$f\left(x\right) = e^{x} - e^{- x} - e^{- 2x}$

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = e^{x} + e^{- x} + 2e^{- 2x}$

Clearly,~$f^{'} \left(x\right) > 0 \forall x \in \mathbb{R} \left(∵ e^{x} & e^{- x} > 0 \forall x \in R\right)$

So, here~$f \left($x\right)$~is~increasing and $f \left($0\right) = - 1$and clearly~g\left($x\right)$~is decreasing function because it is reciprocal function.

From the graph, we can say that~number~of real roots~$= 2$

$

questions.q:
Let $f: \left[2, 4\right] \to \mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function such that \left(x\log_{\mathrm{e}}x\right)f^{'} \left(x\right) + \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}$x\right)f\left(x\right) + f\left(x\right) ≥ 1, x \in \left[2, 4\right]$ with $f\left(2\right) = $\dfrac{1}{2}and $f\left(4\right) = $\dfrac{1}{2}.
Consider the following two statements:

(A)~$f \left(x\right) ≤ 1, \text{for all}x \in \left[2, 4\right]$

(B)~$f \left($x\right) ≥ 1 / 8, $\text{for all}$x \in \left[$2, 4\right]

Then,

$
options: Neither statement $( A )$ nor statement $( B )$ is true
Both the statements $( A )$and $( B )$are true
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

Domain and range of function,

$f: \left[2, 4\right] \to \mathbb{R}$

\left(x\log_{\mathrm{e}}x\right)f^{'} \left(x\right) + \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}$x\right)f\left(x\right) + f\left(x\right) ≥ 1, x \in \left[2, 4\right]$

$⇒ \left(x\log_{\mathrm{e}}x\$right)\ddfrac{d}{dx}f\left(x\right) + \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}x\right)f\left(x\right)\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x\right) + $xf\left($x\right)\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}x\right) ≥ 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{d}{dx}\lleft[xlnxf \left($x\right)\right] ≥ 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{d}{dx} \left[$xlnxf \left($x\right)\right] ≥ $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left($x\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{d}{dx}\lleft[$xlnxf\left($x\right) - x\right] ≥ 0$

Hence,~$h ( x ) = $x\left($lnx\right)f\left(x\right) - x$~is a increasing function,

$∴ h ( x ) ≥ h ( 2 ) , x \in [ 2, 4 ]$

$⇒ xlnx $\$timesf\left(x\right) - x ≥ 2ln2 \timesf \left($2\right) - 2$

$⇒ xlnxf ( x ) - x ≥ ln2 - 2$

Similarly,~h\left($x\right) ≤ $h\left($4\right)$

$⇒ $xlnxf\left($x\right) - x ≤ ln4 - 4$

So,~\dfrac{ln2 - 2}{xlnx} + \dfrac{1}{lnx} \lef ($x ) ≤ $\dfrac{ln4 - 4}{xlnx} + \dfrac{1}{lnx}

Now for~$x \in \left[$2, 4\right]$

\dfrac{ln4 - 4}{xlnx} + \dfrac{1}{lnx} \le \dfrac{ln4 - 4}{2ln2} + \dfrac{1}{ln2} =$1 - $\dfrac{1}{ln2}$< 1$

$⇒ f \left(x\right) ≤ 1\text{for}x \in \left[$2, 4\right]$

Now for~$x \in \left[2, 4\right]$

$\dfrac{ln2 - 2}{xlnx} + \dfrac{1}{lnx} \ge \dfrac{ln2 - 2}{4ln4} + \dfrac{1}{ln4} = \dfrac{ln2 - 2}{4ln4} + \dfrac{1}{ln4} = \dfrac{1}{8} + \dfrac{1}{4ln2}> \dfrac{1}{8}$

Hence,~$f ( x ) \ge \dfrac{1}{8}$

Hence both $A$~& $B$~are correct.
Note this question was bonus in Jee Main 2023 April session, as~LMVT on $f ( x ) \cdotxlnx$ can't be satisfied.

Hence, no such $f ( x )$ exist.

Since, given parabola is symmetric about the $y -$ axis, hence rectangle will also be symmetric about $y -$ axis.

Let one vertex of the rectangle on the $x -$ axis be \left(\alpha, 0\right)$, then

Area of rectangle $A = 2\alpha . \left(12 - {α}^{2}\right)$

For area to be maximum, put~$\alpha =2$~in the equation for area of the rectangle, we get

${A}_\max = 2 \times2 \times \left(12 - {2}^{2}\right) = 32$

Now,

So,

$\dfrac{1}{10} \le \dfrac{1}{1 + x^{2}} \le1$

$⇒ \dfrac{21}{10} \lef^{'}\left(x\right) ≤ 3$

And,

$\dfrac{1}{10} \leg^{'}\left(x\right) ≤ 1$

So,~$minf^{'} \left(x\right) = $\dfrac{21}{10} \ne\left[$1 + maxg^{'}\left($x\right)\right]$

Option \left(4\right)$~is incorrect

$g^{'} \left(x\right) < f^{'} \left(x\right) \forall x \in \left[0, 3\right]$

Since,~$f^{'} \left($x\right)$~and~$g^{'} \left(x\right)$~are~both positive so $f \left(x\right)$~and~$g \left(x\right)$ both are increasing

So,

questions.q: Suppose $f  \left(x\right)$ is a polynomial of degree four having critical points at $- 1, 0, 1$.~If~$T = \left\{x \in \mathbb{R} | f\left(x\right) = f\left(0\right)\right\}$, then the sum of squares of all the elements of $T is :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
f^{'} \left(x\right) = k . x \left($x + 1\right)\left(x - 1\right)$

$= k \left(x^{3} - x\right)$

Integrating both sides with respect to~$x$, we get

$f\left(x\right) = k\left(\dfrac{x4}{4} - \dfrac{x2}{2}) +$c$

$⇒ f \left($0\right) = c$

$∵ $f\left($x\right) = $f\left($0\right)$

$⇒ $k\left($x^{4} - 2x^{2}\right)4 + c = c$

$⇒ $x^{2}\left($x^{2} - 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = 0, $\sqrt{2}, - \sqrt{2}

$⇒ T = \left\{0, $\sqrt{2}, - \sqrt{2}\right

Thus, sum of squares of all the elements of~$T$~is~ \left($0\right)2 + \left(\sqrt{2}\right)$2 + \left(- \sqrt{2}\right)$2 = 4$.

questions.q: If the absolute maximum value of the function $f \left(x\right) =  \left($x^{2} - 2x + 7\right)e\left(4x^{3} - 12x^{2} - 180x + 31\right)$in the interval  \left[-3, 0\right]$~is $f \left(\alpha\right),$then
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f \left(x\right) = \left($x^{2} - 2x + 7\right)e\left(4x^{3} - 12x^{2} - 180x + 31\right)$

Now differentiating the function to find function is increasing or decreasing,

$f^{'} \left($x\right) = e \left(4x^{3} - 12x^{2} - 180x + 31\right)\left(12\left(x^{2} - 2x - 15\right) + 2\left(x - 1\right)\right)$

$⇒ f^{'} \left(x\right) = e \left($4x^{3} - 12x^{2} - 180x + 31\right)\left(12 \left(x + 3\right) \left($x - 5\right) + 2 \left($x - 1\right)\right)$

$⇒ f^{'} \left($x\right) < 0$~for~$x \in \left[- 3, 0\right]$

So,~$f \left(x\right)$is decreasing function on~ \left[-3, 0\right]$

The absolute maximum value of the function $f \left(x\right)$~is at $x = - 3$

$⇒ \alpha = -3$

questions.q:

(S2) $f(x)$ is decreasing in  \left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]$ and increasing in  \left[\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right]$.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & f^{\prime}(x)=\cos x-x+1 \\ & f^{\prime}(x)=-\sin x-1\end{aligned}\mathrm{f}$ is decreasing $\forall \mathrm{x} \in \mathrm{R}$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=0 \\ & \mathrm{f}(0)=2, \mathrm{f}(\pi)=-\pi\end{aligned}$\mathrm{f}$ is strictly decreasing in $[0, \pi]$ and $\mathrm{f}(0) . \mathrm{f}(\pi) \lt 0\Rightarrow$ only one solution of $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=0\mathrm{S} 1$ is correct and $\mathrm{S} 2$ is incorrect.

Then maximum value will be

questions.q: The number of distinct real roots of the equation $3x^{4} + 4x^{3} - 12x^{2} + 4 = 0$& is _________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$3x^{4} + 4x^{3} - 12x^{2} + 4 = 0$

So,~

let~$f \left($x\right) = 3x^{4} + 4x^{3} - 12x^{2} + 4$

$∴ f^{'} \left($x\right) = 12x\left($x^{2} + x - 2\right)$

$= 12x \left(x + 2\right) \left(x - 1\right)$

$f\left(0\right) = 4$

$f\left(1\right) = - 1$

Ans.~$4$

$

questions.q: Let $\mathrm{A}$ be the region enclosed by the parabola $y^2=2 x$ and the line $x=24$. Then the maximum area of the rectangle inscribed in the region $\mathrm{A}$ is________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & A=2\left(24-\frac{b^2}{2}\right) \cdot b \\ & \frac{d A}{d b}=0 \quad \Rightarrow \quad b=4 \\ & A=2(24-8) 4 \\ & =128\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let the function $f  \left(x\right) = 2x^{2} - \log_{\mathrm{e}}x, x > 0$, be decreasing in \left(0, a\right)$~and increasing in  \left(a, 4\right)$. A tangent to the parabola $y^{2} = 4ax$~at a point $P$ on it passes through the point  \left(8a, 8a - 1\right)$~but does not pass through the point  \left(- $\dfrac{1}{a},0\right)$. If the equation of the normal at $P$~is $\dfrac{x}{α} + \dfrac{y}{β} =1$, then $\alpha + \beta$ \text{ and } is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $f\left(x\right) = 2x^{2} - \log_{\mathrm{e}}x$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(x\right) = 4x - \dfrac{1}{x}$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{4x^{2} - 1}{x}$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(x\right) = 0 ⇒ 4x^{2} - 1 = 0 ⇒ x = \pm \dfrac{1}{2}$

But given~$x > 0\text{so}x = \dfrac{1}{2}$

So function is decreasing in~ \left(0, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$~and increasing~in the interval~ \left(\dfrac{1}{2}, \infty\right)$

So,~$a = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Now equation of parabola will be~$y^{2} = 2x$

Now tangent to~$y^{2} = 2x$~will be given by,

$y = mx + \dfrac{1}{2m}$, given this tangent passes through~ \left(8a, 8a - 1\right) ≡ \left(4, 3\right)$,

So~$3 = 4m + $\dfrac{1}{2m}

$⇒ m = $\dfrac{1}{2}\text{or}\dfrac{1}{4}

So equation of tangent are~$y = $\dfrac{x}{2} ++$1\text{or}$y = \dfrac{x}{4} +2$

But~$y = \dfrac{x}{2} +1$~passes through~ \left(-$2, 0\right)$~so rejected as given in the question.

Now equation of normal at~$P$~will be,

$y = - 4x - $2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(-$4\right) - $\dfrac{1}{2} \left(-$4\right)3$~\left\{\text{as slope of normal =}\dfrac{- 1}{\dfrac{1}{4}}\text{=-4}\right

$⇒ y = - 4x + 4 + 32$

$⇒ y + 4x = 36$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{9} + \dfrac{y}{36} =1$

So,~\alpha =$9, $\beta =$36$

So,~\alpha + \beta =$45

questions.q:
In the figure, ${θ}_{1} + {θ}_{2} = \dfrac{π}{2}$ and $\sqrt{3} \left(BE\right) = 4 \left($AB\right)$. If the area of $∆ CAB$ is 2\sqrt{3} -$3{unit}^{2}$, when \dfrac{\theta2}{\theta1}is the largest, then the perimeter (in unit)$ of ∆ CED$ is equal to

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

And& ${θ}_{1} + {θ}_{2} = \dfrac{π}{2}$

Now, Let~$AB = x, BD = y$

Also given,~$\sqrt{3}BE = 4AB$

$⇒ \sqrt{3}\left(y + DE\right) = 4x$

$⇒ DE = \dfrac{4x}{3} - y$

Now given area of triangle~$∆ CAB = 2\sqrt{3} - 3$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}xy = 2\sqrt{3} - 3$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{4\sqrt{3} - 6}{x}$

Now finding,

${tanθ}_{2} = \left(\dfrac{4x}{3} - y\right)x = \dfrac{4}{3} - \dfrac{( 4\sqrt{3} - 6 )}{x2}$

${tanθ}_{1} = \dfrac{y}{x} = \dfrac{4\sqrt{3} - 6}{x2}$

Now taking~$tan$~both of~${θ}_{1} + {θ}_{2} = \dfrac{π}{2}$~we get,

${tanθ}_{1} \cdot {tanθ}_{2} = 1$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{4}{3} - \dfrac{4\sqrt{3} - 6}{x2}\right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{4\sqrt{3} - 6}{x2}\right) = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{4\sqrt{3} - 6}{x2} = \sqrt{3}or\dfrac{1}{3}$

So,~$\dfrac{\theta2}{\theta1}$ is maximum when~$\dfrac{4\sqrt{3} - 6}{x2} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ x^{2} = \sqrt{3} \lleft(4\sqrt{3} -6)$

$⇒ x^{2} = 12 - 6\sqrt{3}$

$⇒ x^{2} = \left(3 - \sqrt{3}\right)2$

$⇒ x = 3 - \sqrt{3}$and~${θ}_{2} = 60 °$

$⇒ \tan 60 ° = \dfrac{DE}{CD}⇒ DE = x \cdot \sqrt{3} ==3\sqrt{3} -$3$

And~$\cos 60 ° = $\dfrac{CD}{CE}$⇒ CE = 2x = 6 - $2\sqrt{3}

So, the Perimeter of~$∆ CED = CD + DE + CE = 6$

$
